Validation Caveats

Holdout-year prediction is evaluated on 2025 observations. Predictors in the test set may be contemporaneously observed rather than known before the forecast date. This is a conditional prediction assessment, not proof of fully prospective forecasting.

Traditional residual normality and heteroskedasticity tests are descriptive when pharmacy-month records are dependent. Very high VIF indicates multicollinearity requiring attention.

Out-of-Sample Predictions

Observed vs. predicted values for the 2025 holdout set, with row-level auditability.

Methodology, Quality & Licensing

Model Assumptions

Financial: sales and COGS scale with selected sales growth; operating expenses follow the selected expense change; each additional pharmacist (network-wide total) costs 18,000 SAR per month (synthetic assumption); waiting time uses per-pharmacy staffing of 3.33 + n/120.

Waiting time: baseline waiting time × (baseline pharmacists / adjusted pharmacists)1.25 × (1 + 0.15 × sales growth), floored at five minutes. This is an illustrative approximation, not a calibrated queueing system.

Inventory: availability and stockout are scenario targets, not predicted outcomes. No causal effect is claimed.

Forecast trend: the six-month comparison uses the historical monthly seasonality profile to vary projected sales and waiting-time context. These are illustrations, not statistically validated forecast intervals.

Quality Assurance from Original Statistical Work

Checks were reported by the prior analytical scripts. This HTML validates its own data counts and financial identity separately on load.

Changelog

v1.1 — 11 Nov 2026

  • Staffing grain fix: financial totals are network-level (120 pharmacies) while baseline staffing is the per-pharmacy average (3.33). The previous version added only 18,000 SAR for each pharmacist while applying the waiting-time effect as if every pharmacy received that pharmacist, which overstated profit in staffing scenarios. “Additional Pharmacists” is now the network-wide total: cost = n × 18,000 SAR/month; waiting-time effect uses the per-pharmacy average (3.33 + n/120).
  • Scenarios redefined at realistic network scale: S2 +12, S3 +24, S4 +36 pharmacists (previously 2, 2 and 3 per pharmacy, which would cost 4.3–6.5M SAR/month).
  • Baseline stockout now uses the observed 2025 mean (5.96%) instead of 1 − availability (5.97%).
  • Diagnostics filter now includes FLAG (5 results).

Known limitations for review: the waiting-time formula (exponent 1.25, growth factor 0.15) is an assumption, not estimated from data (waiting-time model R² = 0.12); some synthetic rows have availability + stockout > 100% (max 103.6%) and utilization up to 206%.
